Think of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model like a specialized traffic control center. Instead of one massive computer handling every single intersection simultaneously, you have a team of specialized experts. When a car approaches an intersection, the system only wakes up the specific experts needed for that exact scenario—like those handling left turns or school zones—while leaving others asleep.

This "sparse activation" is why MoEs run on laptops. Traditional models force every part of the brain to work for every task, draining battery and heat. MoEs only activate a tiny fraction of the total parameters for each query. It’s the difference between running a marathon and taking a short walk. By processing only what’s necessary, the model delivers high intelligence with a fraction of the computational power, making advanced AI feasible
